BiblicalUsage: Nebushazban is named once, among the princes of Babylon sent to fetch Jeremiah out of the court of the prison when Jerusalem falls. He is the chief of the eunuchs, standing beside Nebuzaradan when the prophet is released.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe even the enemy's officers serve God's purposes: the chief eunuch of Babylon is the one sent to loose Jeremiah, and the prophet's freedom comes through the hands that bound his city.
